messages.author: e0346f03a32e14df
messages.subject: error model using Ornitella units
parts:
Greetings

I attended a CTMM workshop a few weeks at at the national TWS meeting and was very impressed.  Thank you Chris and Mike!

My questions relate to calibrating units and implementing that in an error model.  First, in this instance, I'm studying mallards using Ornitella 20g GPS-GSM transmitters.  Most data is collected hourly and we believe the potential scale of error is greater than the scale of movement,  in some cases at least.  

First question, I see in this paper that you tested these exact units but you indicate "NA" when reporting the RMSE.  Is this because the units you tested had much variability among them?  Or some other reason? 

Second question.  I have ample calibration data from 16 units and I can calculate an RMSE on each.  My apologies if this is clear in the help files but could you explain how I translate an RMSE to HDOP and ultimately how I implement this within the uere.fit function?  

Much appreciated in advance!

Jake Straub


Jacob N. Straub, PhD
Senior Research Associate
Research Foundation for State University of New York (SUNY)
Department of Environmental Science and Ecology
SUNY Brockport
jst...@brockport.edu

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: error model using Ornitella units
parts:
Hi Jacob.

The reported RMSE_min is the RMSE under ideal satellite reception (usually HDOP=1). However, those tags did not have informative HDOP values, and the selected error model was the homoskedastic one. Therefore your RMSE would be environmentally dependent.

Following the error vignette, you would run uere.fit() on the calibration data and then uere()<- to calibrate. However, with this model tag, I would definitely do error-model selection and test to see if the HDOP values are informative. There is a good chance that you would want to toss them out (opposite to the vignette example).

Best,
Chris
